2. Declared application, interfaces and remaining useful load

The application is a nonoccupied factory equipment frame carrying a compact handling or indexing fixture. It uses designed-in service tracks and replaceable joint contacts. It is not presented as an arbitrary legacy retrofit.

The joint frame has 
𝑥

𝑧
z vertical. The required total wrench includes the moving frame, service interfaces, tools and their reactions.

Two substantive joint families
Feature	Bolted face	Moment-carrying strut end
Main geometry	Two 240 × 240 × 30 mm flanges	80 mm tongue inside an 86 mm clear socket, 180 mm outside
Separation/access provision	Permanent 3 mm face gap	Radial/end clearance with an open lower access region
Main retention	Four M12 class 10.9 bolts	Independent keys and retention pins
Load contacts	Four removable bearing/nut cartridges and two Ø16 mm shear pins	Eight keys at two stations 130 mm apart; edge contacts carry torsion
Removal travel	Shear pins withdraw 45 mm	Keys withdraw 55 mm radially; retaining pins withdraw 230 mm
Critical requirement	Bolts, bearing lands and shear pins must all leave	Keys and pins must leave without treating the tongue as a freely pivoting clevis

The face bolts have a proposed 25 kN preload, with a 15–35 kN admitted range. The strut includes structural caps and bolts rather than relying on an inadequately preloaded friction clamp.

Both designs preserve a useful unloaded withdrawal path in their nominal geometry. The complete tool, reaction-bar, keeper, cable and brace sweeps have not all been closed. The report distinguishes checked component envelopes from unfinished assembled routes.
